First, I usually text Julia every night. That's a routine we've established, and it's probably a way we stay connected. It's something we both expect and rely on, I think. Maybe I thought she wouldn't be able to respond because she's setting up her new phone. Or perhaps I assumed she might be busy with the new device and wouldn't want to be disturbed. Alternatively, maybe I was worried that she might not have her messages synced yet, so she wouldn't receive my text. But wait, is that a valid reason? I mean, people usually can still receive texts even if they're setting up a new phone, right? Unless she's in the middle of a factory reset or something, but that's probably a short period. Maybe I thought she'd prefer some space to get used to the new device without distractions. But then again, if we usually text every night, she might expect it and feel a bit left out if I don't. I should also consider Julia's perspective. How would she feel if I didn't text her? If she's excited about her new phone, she might have wanted to share that with me. Or she might have been looking forward to our usual conversation. By not texting, I might have missed an opportunity to connect with her about something important to her. On the other hand, maybe I thought she was busy, and I didn't want to impose. But if that's the case, perhaps a quick message checking in would have been better. It shows that I care about her well-being and am considerate of her situation. So, putting it all together, not texting Julia because she got a new phone might not be the best decision.
